short: The world's first battlecruiser, designed with battleship armament but cruiser speed at the expense of heavy armour.
full:
Commissioned on 20 March 1909, HMS Invincible was the pioneer of Admiral John 'Jackie' Fisher's battlecruiser concept. She carried the heavy 12-inch guns of a dreadnought battleship but sacrificed thick armour plating to achieve the high speed of a cruiser. The theory dictated that she could outrun any ship she could not outgun, and outgun any ship she could not outrun.

The flaws in this doctrine were fatally exposed at the Battle of Jutland on 31 May 1916. While serving as the flagship of the 3rd Battlecruiser Squadron, Invincible took a direct hit from the German battlecruiser SMS Lützow on her 'Q' turret. The impact ignited her magazines, causing a catastrophic explosion that tore the ship in half, sinking her in ninety seconds with the loss of over a thousand men.
